resources.string: Emufii: Azahar and Eden netplay filling
Lets Emufii fill in the connection address in Azahar\'s or Eden\'s multiplayer menu, so you don\'t have to retype it. Emufii only watches those two emulators, and only while a session is running.
Filters the library as you type, across every console.
Grid, carousel or list. The list is the one that tells two dumps of a game apart.
A → Z, recently added, or by console: sorting by console files the library into folders.

Your name, your avatar and your friend code. And every app setting.

Hidden from the session list. Your code lets people in.
Shows in the session list. Anyone can join.
You play with strangers, on a public server run by third parties. Emufii creates no session and brings up no tunnel: it opens PPSSPP, and PPSSPP is what connects you.
To do, once and for all
First exit any running PSP game to PPSSPP’s menu. Then use the button below and go to Settings → Networking.
Turn networking on, and pick a public server from the list PPSSPP keeps up to date.
Leave “Try to use the server’s packet relay” on Automatic: that is what public servers want. Emufii switches this game back to private-session values automatically when needed.
Come back here and launch the game, then take its ad hoc mode.

Emufii sets up remote multiplayer between emulators: it shares a network, it doesn\'t reimplement any game. Distributed under the AGPL 3.0 licence, it never routes to Nintendo\'s official servers and ships no ROMs, no BIOS and no keys.
Emufii can fill the address into the emulator\'s multiplayer menu, so you have nothing to copy out.
Emufii cannot fill the emulator\'s form in. Sessions still work, the address just has to be typed by hand.

Nintendo\'s servers have been off since 2014. Kaeru WFC is a third-party reimplementation that replays the original protocol. Emufii points melonDS\'s lookups at it, and nothing else on the device is affected.

Emufii tells you when a friend comes online or starts a game, and when a new version is out. Outside the app an alert can arrive up to a quarter of an hour late: with no push service, Android only wakes the app at intervals.

Pick PPSSPP\'s memory-stick root: the folder holding PSP/SYSTEM/ppsspp.ini. Android grants access to that one only.
